## Summary

The failure was caused by the urllib3 2.0 upgrade. In urllib3 2.0, `HTTPConnectionPool._make_request()` calls `conn.request(method, url, body=..., headers=..., chunked=..., preload_content=..., decode_content=..., enforce_content_length=...)`. urllib3 2.0 therefore expects pooled connection objects to subclass `urllib3.connection.HTTPConnection`, which implements that new signature.

Docker's custom transports (`UnixHTTPConnection`, `NpipeHTTPConnection`, `SSHConnection`) subclassed `http.client.HTTPConnection`, whose `request()` accepts none of those keyword arguments — hence `TypeError: HTTPConnection.request() got an unexpected keyword argument 'chunked'` when `APIClient.build()` (via the Unix socket adapter) tried to send its request body.

Fix (in `docker/transport/unixconn.py`, and the identically-affected `npipeconn.py`/`sshconn.py` for consistency): change the connection classes to subclass `urllib3.connection.HTTPConnection` instead of `http.client.HTTPConnection`, keeping the existing `connect()` overrides that attach the unix/npipe/ssh socket. This makes `getresponse()` return a proper urllib3 `HTTPResponse` (whose `_fp` is the underlying `http.client` response), which is what docker's `_stream_helper`/`_multiplexed_*` helpers and requests already expect.
